description.narrative:
The Government launched the second phase (2020-2023) of the Productive Social Safety Net Programme (PSSN II), under the Tanzania Social Action Fund (TASAF). This is a multi-donor funded social protection programme implemented in 187 districts targeting 1.4 million poorest and most vulnerable households, with a focus on rural areas. The objective is to improve access to income-earning opportunities and socio-economic services for targeted households while enhancing and protecting the human capital of their children.
TASAF executed an Employment Impact Assessment (EmpIA) study in 2020 with an objective of assessing the employment and livelihoods opportunities in three agricultural value chains: cashew nuts, grapes and cotton. The study resulted in the development of guidelines for interventions under the Public Work (PW) component to maximize employment opportunities in the value chains.
The Tanzania Rural and Urban Authority (TARURA), adopted in August 2020 a community based rural road maintenance strategy and developed a technical manual to guide the process. In addition, TARURA and the Institute of Construction Technology (I-COT) adopted, in July 2020, an innovative employment-intensive approach for rural and urban infrastructure development.
The Government of Tanzania designed the seven year - (2021 -2027) ‘Roads to Inclusion and Socio-Economic Opportunities (RISE) Programme', approved by the World Bank Board on May 2021. The main objective of the programme is to stimulate local economic growth and reduce poverty through improved rural accessibility and strengthening the capacity of rural roads sector institutions. The ILO through, with support from the Irish cooperation, contributed to the PSSN II interventions through: training of 218 (76 male & 142 female) TASAF staff at different levels; development of 10 technical and management tools; and supporting monitoring and coordination of the programme activities that resulted in increased ownership and sustainability. The ILO also provided technical to undertake the EmpIA study and the development of a guideline that was adopted and rolled out by TASAF. The guideline helps in the optimization of inputs investment for maximum results, through estimation of possible impacts on employment of increased national sales by PSSN II Programme beneficiaries.
The ILO supported the Government to execute an assessment on inclusiveness of public procurement systems, procedures and legal frameworks. With Irish funding, the ILO provided support to TARURA in the development of a strategy and technical guidelines on community-based routine maintenance of roads and in mainstreaming gender in the road infrastructure development in rural areas.
The ILO also developed the capacity of 43 (29 male & 14 female) staff from relevant public institutions and implementation partners (TARURA, Appropriate Technology Training Institute -ATTI, I-COT, Tanzania National Roads Agency – TANROADS, TASAF and Ministry of Works) on the application of Employment Intensive investment approach for rural and urban infrastructure development.
The ILO in collaboration with the World Bank, supported the conceptualisation and design of the "Roads to Inclusion and Socio-Economic Opportunities (RISE) Programme (2021-2027)" by facilitating missions to project areas, developing knowledge documents and information, and supporting TARURA on the preparatory activities including training of their staff and development of technical and managerial tools.

description.narrative:
The National Bureau of Statistics in close collaboration with the Prime Minister's Office-Labour, Youth, Employment and Persons With Disabilities (PMO-LYED), conducted the National Integrated Labour Force Survey (ILFS), whose planning started back at the beginning of the biennium in 2020, conforming to the to the 19th ICLS standards and methods
PMO-LYED is finalizing mapping of Youth Employment Initiatives in the country (started in June 2020) to inform policies and strengthen co-ordination of youth employment initiatives and national database for youth employment interventions in the country. Within the UN One fund project, the ILO in collaboration with World Bank, supported the National Bureau of Statistics to plan, develop the questionnaire and sampling for the 2020 Integrated Labour Force Survey. Technical support was provided and stakeholder consultations undertaken to integrate a component on time use into the questionnaire, analysing the amount of time people spend doing unpaid and non-market related work.
